headline: Frozen pizza competition intensified at Walmart and Target while category dollars declined; Real Dough needs sharper value proof, retailer-ready product data and a defendable sourdough quality story.

items: Market intel feed is current through 2026-08-28 with five daily reports for ISO week 35.
Premium artisan pizza can still scale: PORTA expanded handmade Roman-style frozen pizzas to Target nationwide and online, reaching 4,500 U.S. retail doors at an $11.99 price point.
Target food and beverage momentum is real: Q2 2026 sales grew 7.2% YoY to just under $6B after a broad grocery reset.

Hospitality reputation signal remains healthy across the Merriment Social group: Google ratings in data/reviews.json are 4.4 Merriment Social, 4.5 Third Coast Provisions, 4.5 Flourchild Pizza and 4.7 The Loon Room.

Frozen pizza is a share-capture fight, not a category tailwind: Circana data cited this week shows U.S. frozen pizza sales down 2.4% to $7.3B, while Palermo Villa grew 10% and Champion Foods grew 17%.
Functional and better-for-you claims are moving into direct pizza competition: CAULIPOWER launched a High Protein Supreme Pizza at Walmart with 42g protein, 6g fiber and an $8.26 SRP.
Private-label acceptance is broad: 58% of consumers say brand type does not matter if the product meets the need; 68% view private label as a good alternative to national brands.

Prepared foods keep encroaching on the same meal occasion: Kroger is expanding Ukrop's prepared-food sections, Redner's is adding restaurant-style Fresh Market formats, and young parents are buying prepared foods weekly.
Build buyer-facing value proof against private label and prepared-food alternatives: price per meal, ingredient quality, sourdough differentiation, convenience and family-occasion fit.

Audit every retailer PDP and sell sheet for clean-label, nutrition, protein, fiber, prep-time, serving-size, origin and sourdough-process claims; missing attributes now weaken search, substitution and buyer confidence.
Pressure-test Real Dough's Walmart/Target story against CAULIPOWER's functional $8.26 pizza and PORTA's $11.99 Target rollout; decide where Real Dough wins and where claims need tightening.

Ask agency for first-frame creative that makes the at-home meal value obvious: real sourdough, premium ingredients, fast prep and better-than-takeout positioning. Do not claim creative performance until the current analytics source is wired into this repo.

agency_brief.what_worked: The defensible story this week is premium pizza with proof. PORTA shows a slow-fermented, artisan pizza can earn national Target distribution at a premium price, and Target's grocery growth shows discovery-led retail still has room for strong frozen brands.
agency_brief.what_didnt: Generic premium positioning is not enough. Category dollars are down, private label is accepted as a practical substitute, and competitors are using explicit functional claims, price architecture and prepared-meal convenience to win the same occasion.
agency_brief.recommendation: Make Real Dough easier to justify at shelf and online: lead with real sourdough process, Wisconsin origin, clean ingredient proof, fast at-home meal utility and a clear value argument versus private label, prepared foods and functional frozen pizza competitors.
agency_brief.competitive_context: CAULIPOWER is bringing a 42g-protein gluten-free pizza to Walmart at $8.26; PORTA is scaling Roman-style, 24-hour slow-fermented pizza through Target at $11.99; frozen pizza dollars are down 2.4% while selected challengers gain share; and grocery retailers are pushing private label, prepared foods and digital product execution harder.

missing: Current paid/social/content analytics source is not wired into this repo; no weekly campaign-performance or creative-winner claims were made.
No current Real Dough sales, velocity, distribution, promo-performance or retailer PDP-completeness feed is available from the approved current sources for this run.
